Propellerhead Reason, 2000

Music software drawn as a studio equipment rack, with a back panel of animated patch cables.

Source
Sound On Sound, Derek Johnson and Debbie Poyser, review (March 2001)
Creator
Propellerhead Software (now Reason Studios)
Made
First released in 2000
Style
Skeuomorphism (precursor; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Technical, mechanical, tactile
Evidence
No image was inspected. Based on the Sound On Sound review (March 2001) and Wikipedia.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Reason first released in 2000. “Reason simulates a recording studio with virtual cables and representations of a subtractive synthesizer, sampler and drum machine.” Wikipedia: Reason Studios.

Sound On Sound: devices “appear as graphic units in a rack”; “flipping the on-screen image reveals a back-panel view of the virtual hardware, complete with animated pluggable cabling.” Audio cables are red, effects cables green, and Gate and CV leads yellow. The mixer’s look “owes a lot to Mackie’s LM3204.” Sound On Sound, March 2001.

Wikipedia’s skeuomorph article names audio software that emulates “physical musical instruments and audio equipment complete with buttons and dials” as an extreme example. Wikipedia: Skeuomorph.

Why it belongs

Here the metaphor carries function: the cable view is how users route signals. It is the strongest case for the style’s claim that familiar objects teach.
